newsitem.title: USA: Japan to start testing PLC heart laser.
newsitem.headline: Japan to start testing PLC heart laser.

text.p: PLC Systems Inc said on Tuesday the Japanese Ministry of Health and Welfare would begin immediate clinical studies of the company's heart laser system at 10 leading Japanese university hospitals.
The company also said it would ship another two heart lasers to IMATRON Japan Inc in the fourth quarter for the clinical studies.
IMATRON told PLC that the Japanese Ministry of Health and Welfare was expected to approve the heart laser in late 1997, PLC Systems said.

The company shipped six heart lasers to IMATRON in December 1995 to begin research and pre-clinical studies of its new cardiosurgical procedure known as its transmyocardial revascularization using the laser.

PLC Systems is a cardiac revascularization company developing medical systems to provide patients with coronary artery disease a third alternative or adjunct to angioplasty and cardiac bypass surgery.
Its PLC Medical Systems Inc subsidiary developed the C02 Heart Laser, which used PLC's patented 'heart-synchronized pulsed laser' technology for a transmyocardial revascularization, the company said.

PLC said it had been granted expedited review of its PreMarket Approval application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for transmyocardial revascularization using the laser, to treat patients with medically refractory angina who are not candidates for angioplasty or bypass surgery.
